goal: Deliver a CLI-owned, provider-observed, rehearsed Callisto self-release lifecycle that can safely publish or recover the exact merged version without a second approval.
architecture: Callisto-model owns serializable identity, provenance, provider observation, and receipt types; callisto-graph owns fresh derivation, provider-neutral state transition rules, and capability-gated effects; callisto-cli owns the single release lifecycle command surface. GitHub Actions becomes a deliberately thin adapter that checks out current orchestration and explicit source separately, transports artifacts, injects credentials only into execute, and invokes the CLI. Remote providers plus the immutable run envelope are recovery authority; local state is crash evidence only.
tech_stack: Rust workspace: callisto-model, callisto-graph, callisto-cli, callisto-vcs
GitHub Actions, GitHub Releases, artifact attestations
Cargo crates.io, npm registry, PyPI, Git

tasks.title: Freeze the release contract and retire misleading interim claims
steps: Record the owner decisions: merge is approval; no Environment gate; registry duplication is never a recovery strategy; product-level GitHub Release contains binary assets; signing and notarization are deferred; no compatibility-only legacy path is retained before v1.
Classify existing branch work as retained foundations (no approval, dependency repair, terminality failure) versus interim-only work (unconsumed profiles and workflow-owned recovery provenance).
Delete or explicitly mark every unconsumed release-profile and workflow-only recovery contract as interim before the canonical implementation starts; do not leave two semantic authorities.
Make documentation and static policy checks reject reintroduction of an approval gate without claiming they prove runtime release behavior.
tasks.commit_message: docs(release): establish the self-release lifecycle contract

tasks.title: Introduce canonical recovery, observation, and receipt domain types
steps: Add versioned, serde-validated types for release-run provenance, explicit recovery request, provider observations, operation evidence, and terminal receipt; preserve forward-compatible identifiers without serializing credentials or raw secret endpoints.
Represent absent, exact success, conflict, and indeterminate observation as non-overlapping states so callers cannot turn uncertainty into success.
Make the receipt constructor reject incomplete, conflicted, or indeterminate operation evidence and test invalid JSON, stable ordering, digest binding, and all rejected states.
tasks.commit_message: feat(model): model recoverable release run evidence

tasks.title: Make graph execution converge from provider observation
steps: Define one provider-observer/effect boundary for registry publications, tags, forge releases, and artifact uploads; migrate all operation roles through it rather than retaining ecosystem-specific reconciliation paths.
Reconcile an immutable intent with remote observations before dispatch and immediately before each effect; persist local transition evidence atomically but treat it only as an interruption aid.

Make a fresh-runner resume reconstruct state from run envelope plus observation evidence, mark exact remote effects already satisfied, reject conflicts and indeterminate responses with miette diagnostics, and retain the existing E172 incomplete-state failure.

Add table-driven graph tests for interruption after Attempting, every partial-operation permutation, exact prepublication, conflict, unavailable provider, dependency ordering, fresh state directory, and receipt eligibility.
tasks.commit_message: feat(graph): reconcile releases from provider observations

tasks.title: Replace fragmented release commands with one CLI lifecycle
steps: Replace preview-only plan/reconcile/execute composition with a coherent release lifecycle command family that accepts distinct orchestration revision and source-root/source-revision inputs and writes a run envelope outside the source checkout.

Require recovery-source validation against the managed merged release decision, prevent recovery from invoking versioning, and make normal and recovery runs use the same graph coordinator rather than divergent workflow branches.
Load and validate release profiles through this command surface; remove CLI aliases or code paths that bypass the canonical coordinator before v1.
Test CLI diagnostics for invalid SHA, source/orchestration mismatch, unmanaged source, missing profile, forbidden dry-run execution, missing artifacts, conflicts, and incomplete runs.

tasks.title: Implement binary assets as release operations, not workflow side effects
steps: Make the configured product release declare canonical asset slots for macOS ARM, Linux GNU, Linux musl, and WASI; derive ArtifactUpload operations and their dependency edges in the same intent as registry, tag, and forge operations.

Implement the CLI build/stage command to build from the explicit release source into a temporary directory, generate an intent-bound manifest, verify digests and attestations, and stage no files in the checkout.
Attach only manifest-verified assets to the product-level GitHub Release after the corresponding tag/release observation is exact.

Run target feasibility probes for aarch64-apple-darwin and x86_64-unknown-linux-musl in CI before committing to the final runner/toolchain strategy; preserve a typed unsupported-target failure if a target cannot be built reproducibly.
Do not add Apple signing or notarization; document unsigned macOS artifacts and their verification story.

tasks.title: Turn GitHub Actions into a thin, testable release adapter
steps: Use one checkout of the current default-branch orchestration to build/run Callisto and a separate read-only checkout of the selected release source; pass paths and full revisions to the CLI rather than rebuilding the CLI from the old source.
Keep plan and build credential-free and write-free to providers; give registry tokens and GitHub write capability only to the execute invocation.
Keep all handoff, downloaded artifacts, state evidence, and build outputs under RUNNER_TEMP; assert the source worktree remains clean before and after each CLI invocation.

Reduce workflow shell to argument validation, checkout, artifact upload/download, and one CLI command per lifecycle stage; remove duplicated source validation, provenance JSON construction, and transition logic.
tasks.commit_message: refactor(actions): delegate release semantics to callisto

tasks.title: Add behavioral workflow and provider-adapter tests
steps: Create a hermetic adapter harness using fixture directories and fake provider CLIs/HTTP endpoints so it executes the same CLI arguments, hidden/nested artifact shapes, separate worktrees, and credential boundaries as the workflow without publishing.

Cover a normal run and a recovery run whose orchestration revision differs from its source revision, plus failed publish after Attempting, exact remote success, remote conflict, artifact tampering, missing credentials, and no artifacts in checkout.
Run the harness through just in pull-request CI; retain static YAML checks only for syntax/policy properties that cannot be observed by the harness.

tasks.title: Provision and prove the isolated rehearsal profile
steps: Use the existing private orin-dx/callisto-rehearsal repository as the isolated forge destination; ensure it never shares a production forge repository or registry endpoint.

Select and provision actual isolated Cargo, npm, and PyPI-compatible rehearsal destinations with minimal credentials, or explicitly defer each unsupported provider from rehearsal rather than pretending the forge repository alone is end-to-end coverage.
Add a manual rehearsal dispatch that invokes the same CLI lifecycle under the rehearsal profile and fails closed when required destinations or credentials are absent.
Run one full rehearsal with disposable versions and verify provider state, assets, attestations, receipt, no production writes, and fresh-runner resume.

tasks.title: Enforce merge evidence without recreating manual release approval
steps: Configure the repository ruleset or branch protection to require the named CI, audit, and behavioral-release-harness checks that the release policy relies on; document the exact check names and owner-bypass policy.
Verify that no environment reviewer, deployment protection rule, or workflow input creates a second release approval.
Keep this external configuration change separate from source-code assertions and collect API evidence for the cutover record.
tasks.commit_message: ci: require release evidence before merge

tasks.title: Perform a controlled first recovery and close with external evidence
steps: Reconstruct and verify the selected merged unpublished release source against its committed decision before dispatching recovery; do not assume 0.7.2 is publishable until provider versions, tags, dependency constraints, and source identity are observed again.
Run the rehearsal first, then dispatch a new current-orchestration recovery run for the selected source rather than rerunning any historical workflow.

Verify every registry version, tag target, GitHub Release asset/attestation, provenance envelope, and receipt against the immutable intent; treat any disagreement as an incident, not a successful release.
Only after the independent verification passes, mark the incident closed and prepare the PR.

batches.title: External rehearsal, governance, and release cutover

reasoning: Ordering is driven by semantic dependencies: no Actions rewrite precedes canonical CLI ownership; no rehearsal precedes behavior proof; no production recovery precedes rehearsal and governance evidence.
